title: Vercel MCP now supports Client ID Metadata Documents
description: Any MCP client can now ask to connect to Vercel MCP . You still log in and approve each connection, but the client no longer has to be reviewed by Vercel first. Previously, Vercel reviewed and allowlisted each client and its redirect URIs by hand, and anything not on the list was rejected. To connect, a client publishes a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD), a JSON file on its own domain that describes it, and uses that file's HTTPS URL as its OAuth client_id . This follows the MCP authorization spec, which now recommends CIMD over Dynamic Client Registration. Because Vercel hasn't reviewed these clients, the consent screen shows where each one comes from: its name, its logo, and the hostname that serves its metadata document, for example "Claude Code by claude.ai". CIMD clients don't get the Vercel verified badge, so the hostname is what you're trusting when you approve. Apps already registered with Vercel are unchanged. Read the Vercel MCP documentation to connect your client. Read more

title: Vercel MCP now renders deployments as an interactive card
description: Vercel MCP can now show your deployments as an interactive card inside ChatGPT and other chat clients that support MCP Apps . The card shows live deployment status, build logs, and source and commit details, with a Visit button once the deployment URL is ready. You can send logs into the chat to debug with the model, or open the fullscreen view to read them beneath the card. For repositories linked to multiple projects, a project list lets you switch between them. The card is Vercel MCP's first MCP App, built on the MCP Apps extension. Clients without app support receive the deployment state, preview URL, and commit as text instead. The open_deployments tool looks up deployments by project, repository, or commit, with environment filtering. ChatGPT connects to Vercel MCP through its Connectors setup . Read more

title: Flags Explorer redesigned for easier override sharing
description: Flags Explorer is a tool in the Vercel Toolbar where you can see which feature flags are active on your end, and share them with your team, either by setting them for the branch or through a URL. The Explorer surface has been redesigned to co-locate overrides, branch recommendations, and any related actions. Whenever a branch has overrides set, they will be recommended to teammates visiting the deployment through a dialog. Flags Explorer is available on all plans. Read the documentation to get started. Read more

title: Evaluate Vercel Flags from another project without sharing SDK keys.
description: Project Connections let applications evaluate flags defined in another Vercel project within the same team, without managing SDK keys. Previously, sharing flags between projects required copying a server SDK key into an environment variable and managing it manually. Connected projects authenticate using their deployment’s identity. For local development, vercel env pull retrieves your project’s OIDC token. Manage access from the Connections page under your project's Flags section, or with vercel flags connections in the CLI. Connections grant read-only access across all environments. The consumer deployment determines the flag environment (production deployments evaluate production flags). In the consumer application, create an adapter with the source project’s ID. Access can be revoked without redeploying. Project Connections are available on all plans and require @flags-sdk/vercel 1.6.0 or later, or @vercel/flags-core 1.11.0 or later when using the core library directly. Managing connections from the CLI requires Vercel CLI 63.0.0 or later. Learn more in the Vercel Flags documentation Read more
